Copies what you copy on the device to this phone on its own, and sends this phone\'s clipboard over when you press Ctrl+V on a keyboard, unless the device copied something newer. Turn it off to keep each clipboard private; Copy, Cut and Paste still work when you ask for them.
Locking keeps the mirrored image from turning when the other device is rotated. The device still rotates; only what it sends is held steady. Takes effect on the next connection.

Creates a new display on the remote device and mirrors that instead of its screen, so the device stays usable and its own screen stays private. Needs Android 11 or newer there, and works best on Android 14 or newer. The new display starts empty, so use Apps to open something on it. Takes effect on the next connection.

Device audio silences the remote speaker while mirroring. Playback capture, from Android 13, brings here what apps play and takes it off the device; apps can opt out. With scrcpy 5.0.1 that includes notifications and alarms, and Keep audio playing on the device shares media and games in both places from Android 14.

Keeps the sound playing while the app is off screen. The session itself stays open either way, held behind its notification, so returning is instant; without this only the audio stops.
Signals user activity periodically instead of changing the device\'s own sleep setting, so it works on battery and leaves nothing behind after the session.

Use scrcpy://connect?host=192.168.1.20&port=5555 or scrcpy://192.168.1.20:5555. A valid host and a port from 1 to 65535 are required. Only an omitted port defaults to 5555.\n\nA link may also name a codec, sound, size, frame rate, orientation or screen behaviour. Any value it gives has to be one this app recognises, or the whole link is refused rather than connecting with something you did not ask for.

Step-by-step instructions to enable Wireless debugging
On the phone you want to control, open Settings → About phone, then tap Build number 7 times until Developer options are unlocked.
Connect both phones to the same Wi-Fi network. On the other phone, open Settings → System → Developer options and turn on Wireless debugging.
Tap \"Pair new device\" here, then either scan the QR code from Wireless debugging or tap your phone when it appears in the nearby list.
